newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends largely unscathed by Brash's speech.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends largely unscathed by Brash's speech.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar ended Monday's session largely unscathed by comments from Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash on the currency.
The Kiwi ended at US$0.7079/86 from its 0.7099/06 opening and at 67.33 on the Trade-Weighted Index from 67.54.
Dealers said the decline was more likely to have been a function of the market being long.
Brash told a meeting of Federated Farmers in Southland that the continued rapid rise of the New Zealand dollar would weaken export growth.
One dealer said there was selling pressure from Singapore but that it was easily absorbed. In broad terms, he expected the Kiwi to remain in a 0.7075-0.7130 range.

"I can't get too bearish despite what Brash has said this morning," he said. "Talk is talk and action is action. We have not really seen any action. I can't see it falling away dramatically over the next 24 hours."
Overnight, a 0.7075-05 range was seen but with little action expected due to a holiday in the United States.
Another dealer said the currency had held up well on Friday. "The locals who tried to buy it this morning just caught themselves a little long I think," he said.
"The Brash comments on the day appear to have had only a very minimal impact.
"Two weeks ago, something like that would have caused a drop of 40-50 points fairly sharply, but it's been pretty subdued today."
There was a possibility of an extention to the downside to perhaps 0.7050.
"But overall, it's still the same old thing -- the demand/supply equation. There are just more buyers than sellers," he said.
